messages.content: RULE: Components are NOT standalone. How do you add a component to a scene?
RULE: When asked for C++ code, what should you NOT include?

When asked to write C++ code, respond with PURE C++ CODE ONLY.

Do NOT include:
- !write commands
- !wb-add-ready commands
- !wb-assign commands
- !build commands
- !ipc commands
- Any workboard or tool commands

Those are tool commands for project management. C++ code questions get C++ code answers:

```cpp
// This is what a C++ code answer looks like
auto* cache = GetSubsystem<ResourceCache>();
Node* box = scene_->CreateChild("Box");
auto* model = box->CreateComponent<StaticModel>();
model->SetModel(cache->GetResource<Model>("Models/Box.mdl"));
```

Only use tool commands when explicitly asked to perform a project action like adding a task or building a target.
Create a Scene with Octree and a directional light.
Add a Camera to a scene and set up a Viewport.
Load a mushroom model from ResourceCache and display it.
Write a complete minimal Start() method for a sample application.
DRILL: What is Model vs StaticModel vs AnimatedModel?
DRILL: What is the difference between CreateChild and CreateComponent?

CreateChild(name) — creates a new child NODE in the scene hierarchy. Returns Node*.

CreateComponent<T>() — attaches a new COMPONENT to the current node. Returns T*.

```cpp
// CreateChild makes NODES
Node* child = parentNode->CreateChild("Enemy");   // returns Node*
Node* sub = child->CreateChild("Weapon");          // returns Node*

// CreateComponent attaches COMPONENTS to a node
auto* model = child->CreateComponent<StaticModel>();     // returns StaticModel*
auto* body = child->CreateComponent<RigidBody>();        // returns RigidBody*
auto* light = child->CreateComponent<Light>();            // returns Light*
```

NODES form the scene tree (parent-child). COMPONENTS hang off nodes (flat list per node).
A node can have many children AND many components.
Never confuse the two — they serve completely different purposes.
DRILL: List 5 things that are Resources and 5 things that are Components.

RESOURCES (loaded via ResourceCache::GetResource<T>(path)):
1. Model — mesh data (.mdl files)
2. Material — surface properties (.xml files)
3. Texture2D — image data (.png, .jpg files)
4. Font — text rendering (.ttf files)
5. Sound — audio data (.wav, .ogg files)
6. Animation — skeletal animation (.ani files)
7. XMLFile — XML data

COMPONENTS (attached to Nodes via CreateComponent<T>()):
1. StaticModel — displays a Model
2. AnimatedModel — displays a Model with animations
3. Light — illumination (directional, point, spot)
4. Camera — viewpoint for rendering
5. RigidBody — physics simulation
6. CollisionShape — physics collision geometry
7. SoundSource3D — positional audio playback
8. AnimationController — animation state machine

Resources are data. Components are behavior. Never mix them up.
DRILL: Name all the Urho3D subsystems accessed with GetSubsystem.

Common subsystems (engine singletons):

```cpp
auto* cache     = GetSubsystem<ResourceCache>();  // Asset loading
auto* input     = GetSubsystem<Input>();           // Keyboard/mouse/touch
auto* ui        = GetSubsystem<UI>();              // UI system
auto* graphics  = GetSubsystem<Graphics>();        // Rendering backend
auto* renderer  = GetSubsystem<Renderer>();        // Viewports/passes
auto* audio     = GetSubsystem<Audio>();           // Sound system
auto* network   = GetSubsystem<Network>();         // Networking
auto* fs        = GetSubsystem<FileSystem>();      // File operations
auto* log       = GetSubsystem<Log>();             // Logging
auto* engine    = GetSubsystem<Engine>();          // Engine control
auto* time      = GetSubsystem<Time>();            // Timing
auto* profiler  = GetSubsystem<Profiler>();        // Performance
```

Subsystems are NOT resources. Never GetSubsystem<Font>() or GetSubsystem<Model>(). Those are resources loaded through ResourceCache.
